The main goal is to not generate the format.html block in scaffold
controller, and to generate a different functional test as we don't rely
on redirects anymore, we should test for http responses.

quotes.title: Generate special controller and functional test templates for http apps

quotes.text:
In addition to that, the :edit action is removed from the http
controller and the edit route is not generated by default, as they
usually do not make sense in this scenario.

quotes.text: We've avoided changing all hash syntax since it breaks other pull requests, but maybe it's time! Could you update the tests as well?
quotes.author: jeremy
quotes.title: PR #7941

medium: These passages detail the need to avoid format.html blocks, test http responses, and address issues with edit actions and singleton scaffolds.

card.what: This line sets a configuration option to generate JavaScript files when a Rails generator is run.
card.why: The original intent was to streamline the scaffold generator by avoiding the generation of the `format.html` block and creating functional tests that check HTTP responses instead of relying on redirects. The `:edit` action and associated route were also removed, making this setting crucial for the generator's specific purpose [1][2]. Jeremy suggests updating the tests to align with the current hash syntax [3].
card.next: Before making any changes, verify that the current configuration still aligns with the desired behavior of generating JavaScript files for functional tests.

answer: People should still be able to use CoffeeScript (another JavaScript engine) in generators.
